correctness.rationale: Conditionally on any strictly increasing boundary quadruple, the source evaluation times are independent uniforms on three adjacent intervals. The denominator of \(\beta_k\) is exactly \(\int_{u_{k-1}}^{u_k}2s^{-3}\,ds\), hence is asymptotic to \(2A_k^{-3}(x+y)\) at the unique singular corner \(u_{k-1},u_k\to A_k\). The numerator converges there to the strictly positive quantity \(A_k^{-2}-u_{k+1}^{-2}\). Scaling the two corner coordinates by \(t\) gives a triangular limit region whose area yields the displayed constant. Comparison with \((x+y)^{-p}\) proves the exact \(p=2\) moment threshold. For the randomized boundary schedule, fixed-\(k\) boundary gaps remain in deterministic compact positive ranges, so the conditional \(p<2\) bounds integrate.

value.rationale: The source explicitly highlights that its randomized momentum coefficients can be arbitrarily large, making their size distribution a natural unresolved property of the proposed schedule rather than an arbitrary invariant. The exact \(t^{-2}\) law shows that the coefficients sit precisely at the finite-mean/infinite-variance boundary. This matters for interpretation and implementation of the new acceleration mechanism: ordinary second-moment summaries of the momentum parameter do not exist even though the convergence theorem controls the optimization trajectory. The explicit leading constant also quantifies how local boundary geometry controls extreme momentum events.
